# Your body: a Universal Robots UR16e arm on a parked Clearpath Husky A300

You control a six-joint industrial arm. It is bolted to a wheeled base that is parked and does not move. A socket for 13 mm hex heads is fixed rigidly to the last joint, wrist 3. There is no powered tool: the wrist itself turns the socket.

## Frames and units
- Everything is in SI units: metres, radians, seconds, newtons, newton-metres.
- Base frame: origin at the base of the arm, x forward, y left, z up.
- Tool frame: origin at the centre of the socket's open face, z along the socket's axis, pointing out of the socket.
- An orientation is a unit quaternion in the order x, y, z, w.
- A positive rotation about tool z turns a fastener clockwise as seen from behind the tool. That tightens a right-hand thread.

## Tool
- The socket's face is 0.16 m from the wrist-3 flange, on the wrist-3 axis.
- The socket is a hex 13.3 mm across flats. It only goes over a head whose flats line up with its own, and those repeat every 60 degrees.

## Limits
- Joint torque limits in N·m: shoulder pan 330, shoulder lift 330, elbow 150, wrist 1 54, wrist 2 54, wrist 3 54.
- Joint speed limits in rad/s: shoulder pan and lift 2.094, elbow 3.142, wrists 3.142.
- Wrist 3 turns at most one full turn either way from its zero. A job that needs more rotation than is left has to lift the socket, turn back and seat it again.
- A commanded pose that the arm cannot reach within these limits is not reached. Nothing is done for you.

## Senses
- Joint positions and velocities, and the pose of the tool frame in the base frame.
- A force-torque sensor at the wrist-3 flange gives the force (N) and torque (N·m) that the surroundings apply to the tool, in the tool frame. It reads zero while the tool touches nothing.
- Pressing the socket onto a surface reads as a negative force along tool z.
- While the socket tightens a bolt, the bolt's resistance reads as a negative torque about tool z, equal in size to the tightening torque.

## Commands
You act through the tools you are given: call exactly one tool each turn. The arm moves the tool within its limits and stops when it arrives, when it can go no further, or when the command's time runs out; the tool's result then tells you how the command ended and what the robot senses. Keep calling tools until the job is finished or cannot be finished, then call done.

## Privileged readings
Each round also gives what a scripted controller with full knowledge of the simulation reads:
- head_top_minus_tool: the vector from the centre of the socket's face to the centre of the top of the head.
- bolt_axis: the direction the bolt's axis points out of the head.
- bolt_angle: how far the bolt has been turned in the tightening direction; 0 when it is snug, negative before.
- installed_torque: the tightening torque the bolt has reached (what the job is judged on).
- drive_torque: the torque wrist 3 applies, tightening positive. It is not limited by the force-torque sensor's range.
- engaged: 1 while the socket counts as seated on the head, 0 otherwise.
- where the top of the head is, how deep the socket is on it (said in words), how far and which way the socket is off the bolt's axis, and the angle between them.
- three ready commands: one that centres the socket on the bolt's axis where it is now, one that centres it 0.5 mm out from the head top, and one that puts it 50 mm out on the axis. All point the socket into the bolt and allow for where your last pose actually left the socket (the arm settles a little off its target, consistently the same way).

# Work order: tighten a module clamp bolt

Tighten the clamp bolt in front of the robot into the module manufacturer's torque window, then take the tool away.

The bolt is an M8 with a hex head and a right-hand thread. The centre of the top of its head is at (0.420, 0.015, 0.439) m in the base frame, and its axis points out of the head along (-0.000, 0.342, 0.940). The bolt starts loose, between 149 and 212 degrees short of snug, with its flats at any angle. Installed torque is the tightening torque the bolt has reached; it is near zero until the bolt is snug and rises as the bolt is turned further.

The job is judged on the conditions below, in this order, and on nothing else.
- The socket is seated on the head: the top of the head at least 2.5 mm inside the socket, with the socket's axis within 1.2 mm and 6 degrees of the bolt's.
- The bolt has been turned until it is snug, the point where the clamp starts to resist.
- The installed torque has reached 14 N·m.
- The socket is off the head, its face more than 30 mm from the top of the head.

function.description: Closed loop: turn back slowly, keeping the socket on, until the drive torque is near zero (under 0.1 N·m), so the socket no longer grips the flats. The bolt stays tight. Do this before retract: a socket still loaded grips the flats and the retract sticks.

function.name: retract
function.description: Closed loop: move the socket straight out along the bolt's axis until its face is mm millimetres from the head top, keeping it centred and straight. Unload first. 50 mm or more clears the job's 30 mm condition with a margin.

mm.description: distance of the socket face from the head top, mm

message.reasoning_content: Good, the socket is unloaded (drive torque is 0.08 N·m, under 0.1 N·m). Now I need to retract the socket more than 30 mm from the head top. The retract command will move the socket straight out along the bolt's axis until its face is mm millimetres from the head top. I'll retract to 50 mm which clears the job's 30 mm condition with a margin.
